title: VHS tape tracking and head-switching noise
blurb: An ElementGL WebGL 2 shader degrades a live interactive HTML VCR deck with helical-scan tracking shear, bottom head-switching jitter, YIQ chroma smear and tape dropout snow while keeping transport buttons, channel switches and the tape label input clickable.
question: Can an ElementGL WebGL 2 canvas transform a live interactive HTML broadcast and camcorder player card with analog helical-scan VHS artefacts (tracking dial shear, bottom head-switching jitter, YIQ chroma delay and smear, dropout snow bursts and fast-forward scan streaks) while keeping transport buttons, channel switcher and live text inputs clickable?
result: Measured in headless Chrome 160 Canary (2026-11-27): 6/6 live checks pass on 412 px DPR 2.625 (1.12 MP, 8.97 MB) and 960 px desktop DPR 2 (1.12 MP, 8.97 MB). YIQ chroma bleed measured 144 red 4 px past a sharp edge vs 8 in Clean signal, and updateElementGeometry() kept controls clickable; Chrome 159 on Android and npm run check:jank stay not verified.
